property_summary: For any caller who locks in a guess with exactly 1 ether, calling settle() in the same block as the lock (before the locked block number) must revert, regardless of the guessed hash.
A second lockInGuess call by the same sender while a first guess is still pending must revert, so the stored guess cannot be overwritten.
lockInGuess must revert whenever the caller already has a pending guess (a pre-existing nonzero locked block), so a second lock cannot overwrite an active guess.
After any successful lockInGuess, a subsequent lockInGuess by the same caller reverts, so the test contract's C balance cannot increase from a second lock.
A second lockInGuess from the same address must revert because c only allows a guesser to lock in once while their block field is nonzero.

Since the constructor's 1 ether payment is not counted as a guess, a single lockInGuess of exactly 1 ether succeeds and makes a second lockInGuess from the same address revert, while address(c).balance increases by exactly 1 ether from the first call.

If a guess is locked in and then settled after the target block, the stored guess is cleared (block becomes 0), so a subsequent settle call from the same address must revert because there is no active guess.

After locking in exactly one guess, at most one of the two immediately following settle calls can succeed; settle cannot pay out twice in a row for the same single lock-in because the stored block is cleared on the first successful settle.
After locking in a guess, if the first settle does not revert then the second settle must revert, because a successful settle clears the stored block and makes further settle calls revert.
After lockInGuess, settle never succeeds before the lock's target block has passed, and when it does succeed it pays exactly 2 ether to the solver.
An immediate settle after lockInGuess must revert, because the guess's target block is set to the current block plus one and has therefore not yet passed.
After a successful lockInGuess, the same sender can call settle successfully at most once, and any second settle call reverts because the stored block is cleared.

property_summary: If a guess is locked in and the first settle succeeds, then a second settle by the same sender must revert because a successful settlement clears the stored guess block.

A settle call after lockInGuess cannot succeed at the same block as the lock (target block is future), so if lockInGuess succeeded, settle must revert immediately; equivalently, a successful settle is impossible right after locking.
A second lockInGuess from the same address always reverts once that address has already locked in, regardless of the new value sent.

Calling lockInGuess with exactly 1 ether succeeds and stores the guess, so a subsequent settle before the target block reverts, and the contract retains the locked ether until the guess can be settled.

Calling lockInGuess with 1 ether stores the guess, increases the contract balance by 1 ether, and any immediate settle attempt before the stored target block reverts, leaving the contract balance unchanged.
